## About this dataset

On September 9, 2017, highwinds from Hurricane Irma impacted the Florida Everglades. With 24 hours of heavy rain along with strong winds and storm surge, the storm caused higher than normal water levels, wind-induced defoliation, uprooting of plants and soil disturbance in Everglades short-stature freshwater wetlands. The hurricane redistributed short-stature vegetation into dead mats in Everglades National Park. The high post-storm water levels saturated many of these dead mats, slowing decomposition and increasing their persistence on the landscape. In this study, we measure carbon dioxide (CO2) and methane (CH4) fluxes at dead mats and compared them to the ridge and slough of freshwater marsh and to the marl prairie.

## Variables

`Date` · `Slough` · `Plot` · `Trt` · `NEE` · `GEE` · `Reco` · `Methane_L` · `Methane_D` · `GCB` · `PAR` · `T_Air` · `T_Water` · `Water_Level` · `TSE` · `Substrate` · `Treatment` · `Dry_Mass` · `Fresh_Mass` · `F_Methane` · `F_carbonDioxide` · `Water`

_Units, definitions and uncertainty are documented in the archived metadata (EML)._

## Research applications

- Quantifying greenhouse-gas responses to hurricane disturbance
- Decomposition and recovery after wind and flooding disturbance

## Known limitations

- Campaign-based sampling, not continuous

## Get the data with code

::: {.panel-tabset}
### R

```r
# install.packages("EDIutils")
library(EDIutils)

pkg <- "edi.1150.2"
entities <- read_data_entity_names(pkg)   # list the files in the package
entities

# read the first entity into R
raw <- read_data_entity(pkg, entities$entityId[1])
dat <- readr::read_csv(raw)
```

### Python

```python
import io, requests, pandas as pd

pkg = "edi/1150/2"
base = "https://pasta.lternet.edu/package"
ids = requests.get(f"{base}/data/eml/{pkg}").text.split()
names = requests.get(f"{base}/name/eml/{pkg}").text
print(names)

csv = requests.get(ids[0]).content
df = pd.read_csv(io.BytesIO(csv))
```
